children: Egypt’s exports of chemicals and fertilisers to China surged 678% year on year to $287m during the first eight months of 2026, up from $37m in the same period last year, according to data from the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC).

The strong performance has strengthened China’s position among the top 10 export markets for Egypt’s chemicals and fertilisers sector, as the Egyptian Export Council for Chemical Industries and Fertilizers prepares to participate in the 140th edition of the Canton Fair, scheduled for October 23-27, 2026.

The council will participate through a joint Egyptian pavilion featuring local manufacturers, in coordination with the Egyptian General Authority for International Exhibitions and Conferences and the Egyptian Commercial Office in Beijing.

The initiative aims to expand Egyptian exporters’ access to international markets, facilitate direct engagement with importers and distributors, and establish new commercial partnerships with Chinese buyers.

The sector’s top 10 export markets collectively accounted for 56% of total exports during the reporting period, underscoring the importance of key destinations in supporting the industry’s international expansion.

Khaled Abu El-Makarim, Chairperson of the Egyptian Export Council for Chemical Industries and Fertilizers, said China was becoming increasingly important as a strategic destination for Egyptian exports.
He noted that the sector’s export growth during the January-August period reflected opportunities to expand the presence of Egyptian products in international markets.

“Achieving exports worth $287m to the Chinese market, with growth of 678% compared with the same period last year, reflects a significant improvement in the sector’s export performance and confirms the existence of real opportunities to strengthen the presence of Egyptian products in international markets,” Abu El-Makarim said.

He added that the Egyptian pavilion would bring together manufacturers of glass tableware, decorative glass products and plastic household goods, providing them with an opportunity to showcase their products to international buyers.
The participation forms part of the council’s efforts to support member companies and highlight the diversity, quality and competitiveness of Egypt’s industrial products, he said.

Abu El-Makarim also highlighted the importance of coordination with the Egyptian General Authority for International Exhibitions and Conferences and the Egyptian Commercial Office in Beijing in organising the participation and maximising its benefits.

The cooperation is expected to facilitate direct engagement with international importers and buyers, help Egyptian companies better understand Chinese market demand, and support the development of new business relationships.

The participation marks Egypt’s return to the Canton Fair with a joint pavilion after several years of absence, providing local manufacturers with a platform to showcase their products, connect with international buyers and explore new export opportunities. The initiative supports the council’s efforts to diversify export markets, strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products and build long-term commercial partnerships in China.
